questions.stem: What is the mean of the set 10, 10, 20, 40 and 70?
questions.explanation: The mean adds all the numbers and divides by the count: (10 + 10 + 20 + 40 + 70) / 5 = 30.

questions.stem: What is the median of the set 10, 10, 20, 40 and 70?
questions.explanation: Ordered from lowest to highest, the exact middle value of the five numbers is 20.

options: How variable or spread out the data values are, also called a measure of dispersion from the mean or median
The difference between the largest and smallest table in a database
The number of columns in a dataset
The rate at which data grows each year
The distance between data centres
questions.explanation: Spread is a measure of dispersion: how variable the data values are relative to the mean or median.

questions.stem: In the customer-age example with ages from 10 to 60, what are the mean and median?
options: Mean 30 and median 32
Mean 20 and median 30
Mean 35 and median 35
Mean 40 and median 30
Mean 32 and median 30
questions.explanation: In that dataset the mean is 32 and the median is 30.

questions.stem: In the customer-age example, how is Data Spread expressed in the case of the mean?
options: 30 to 20 and 30 to 60
32 to 20 and 32 to 60
32 to 10 and 32 to 40
questions.explanation: With a mean of 32, the spread is given as 32 to 20 and 32 to 60.

questions.stem: In the customer-age example, how many customers are aged 20?
questions.explanation: The breakdown lists 8 customers aged 10, 15 aged 20, 12 aged 30, 7 aged 40 and 3 aged 60.

questions.stem: How does customer age spread affect content on social media?
options: The more the age is spread, the more types of content must be made
A wider age spread means less content is needed
Age spread only affects advertising prices
Content is unaffected by age spread
A wider spread means content must be shorter
questions.explanation: Content depends on the customer age spread: the wider the spread, the more types of content are required.

questions.stem: How does a larger Data Spread affect a marketing department's campaigns?
options: It reduces the number of campaigns that can run
It makes campaigns impossible to measure
It has no effect on campaigns
It restricts campaigns to a single channel
The greater the spread, the greater the range of campaigns that can be launched and the more customers engaged
questions.explanation: Marketing analysis depends on spread: more spread means a wider range of campaigns and more customer engagement.

questions.stem: Which rule about age groups is given in the social media example of Data Spread?
options: All content must be suitable for every age
Customers over 60 should receive no content
Content should target only the median age
Kids under age 16 should not view content created for older age groups
Content should be made only for the largest age group
questions.explanation: The example notes that children under 16 should not see content created for older age groups.

questions.stem: How is the median of a dataset found?
options: By adding all values and dividing by the count
By ordering the set from lowest to highest and taking the exact middle value
By taking the most frequent value
By subtracting the smallest value from the largest
By averaging the smallest and largest values
questions.explanation: The median is the middle number once the set is ordered from lowest to highest.
